words.enDefinition: a phone number used to contact services that respond to emergencies

examples.en: The local emergency number is printed inside the front cover of our orientation booklet.
examples.zh: 当地的「紧急求助号码」印在我们的迎新手册封面内侧。

examples.en: I saved the campus security desk separately from the national emergency number on my phone.
examples.zh: 我在手机里分别存了校园安保值班电话和全国通用的「紧急求助号码」。

words.enDefinition: a call requesting urgent help from an emergency service

examples.en: The library closed its front doors shortly after staff made an emergency call.
examples.zh: 工作人员打了「紧急求助电话」后不久，图书馆关上了正门。

examples.en: My phone showed the time of the emergency call in its recent calls list.
examples.zh: 我的手机在近期通话列表里显示了拨打「紧急求助电话」的时间。

words.enDefinition: public services that respond to incidents needing urgent help

examples.en: The residence staff notified emergency services after discovering smoke in the laundry room.
examples.zh: 宿舍工作人员发现洗衣房冒烟后，通知了「应急救援部门」。

examples.en: An open gate gave emergency services direct access to the courtyard at night.
examples.zh: 夜里大门开着，「应急救援部门」可以直接进入院子。

words.enDefinition: to telephone someone who can help with an urgent problem

examples.en: My phone had no signal, so I asked the receptionist to call for help.
examples.zh: 我的手机没有信号，就请前台工作人员「打电话求救」。

examples.en: The bus driver stopped by the entrance so a passenger could call for help.
examples.zh: 公交司机把车停在入口旁，好让一名乘客「打电话求救」。

collocations: use a phone to call for help
ask someone to call for help

words.enDefinition: to contact the police by telephone and request assistance

examples.en: The shop assistant offered to call the police while I waited by the till.
examples.zh: 我在收银台旁等着，店员主动提出「打电话报警」。

examples.en: The witness used the station phone to call the police after the crash.
examples.zh: 目击者在事故发生后用车站的电话「打电话报警」。

collocations: ask someone to call the police

words.enDefinition: to telephone the fire service and ask it to attend

examples.en: Her neighbour stepped outside to call the fire brigade after seeing smoke upstairs.
examples.zh: 邻居看到楼上冒烟后走到外面「打电话叫消防队」。

examples.en: The cleaner asked the caretaker to call the fire brigade from the front desk.
examples.zh: 保洁员请管理员用前台的电话「打电话叫消防队」。

collocations: ask someone to call the fire brigade
use a mobile to call the fire brigade

words.enDefinition: to ask for an ambulance by telephone

examples.en: The coach asked another student to call an ambulance from the sports hall.
examples.zh: 教练请另一名学生在体育馆「打电话叫救护车」。

examples.en: I could hear my flatmate call an ambulance from the next room.
examples.zh: 我听见室友在隔壁「打电话叫救护车」。

collocations: ask someone to call an ambulance
use a phone to call an ambulance

words.enDefinition: help provided by the police in dealing with an incident

examples.en: The university staff requested police assistance after reviewing footage of the missing equipment.
examples.zh: 校方工作人员查看设备失踪的监控录像后，请求「警方协助」。

examples.en: The station manager thanked the officer for providing police assistance during the incident.
examples.zh: 车站经理感谢警员在事件中提供了「警方协助」。

words.enDefinition: the organization responsible for responding to fires and related emergencies

examples.en: The fire service visited our residence hall during the campus safety fair.
examples.zh: 在校园安全宣传活动期间，「消防部门」来到了我们的宿舍楼。

examples.en: The fire service sent an officer to speak with the building manager afterward.
examples.zh: 事后，「消防部门」派了一位消防人员和楼宇管理员沟通。

words.enDefinition: an organization that sends ambulances and provides emergency medical transport

examples.en: The ambulance service asked the caretaker to identify the closest accessible entrance.
examples.zh: 「救护车服务机构」请管理员指出最近的无障碍入口。

examples.en: The student newspaper interviewed the local ambulance service about its work on campus.
examples.zh: 学生报采访了当地的「救护车服务机构」，了解他们在校园的工作。

words.enDefinition: a trained person who is among the first to provide emergency help

examples.en: A first responder met us outside the gym and spoke to the coach.
examples.zh: 一名「现场应急人员」在体育馆外与我们会合，并和教练谈了谈。

examples.en: The first witness gave a brief account to the first responder on arrival.
examples.zh: 「现场应急人员」到达后，第一位目击者简要说明了情况。

collocations: provide information to a first responder

words.enDefinition: a centre that answers urgent requests and routes them to responders

examples.en: The emergency call centre transferred the caller to the appropriate local service.
examples.zh: 「紧急电话接听中心」把来电者转接到了当地相关部门。

examples.en: A new shift at the emergency call centre began just before midnight.
examples.zh: 临近午夜，「紧急电话接听中心」的下一班工作人员开始值班。

words.enDefinition: a trained worker who takes calls requesting emergency help

examples.en: The emergency call handler asked her to say the building name again slowly.
examples.zh: 「紧急电话接线员」请她慢一点再说一遍楼名。

examples.en: An emergency call handler checked whether the caller was still near the station.
examples.zh: 一名「紧急电话接线员」确认来电者是否还在车站附近。

collocations: speak to an emergency call handler

words.enDefinition: a worker who sends suitable crews or vehicles to incidents

examples.en: The dispatcher updated the crew when the caller corrected the street name.
examples.zh: 来电者更正街名后，「调度员」把新信息告知了救援人员。

examples.en: A police dispatcher directed the nearest available unit to the station entrance.
examples.zh: 一名警方「调度员」派最近的一组可用警员前往车站入口。

words.enDefinition: the coordination and assignment of responders to urgent incidents

examples.en: I shadowed a member of the emergency dispatch team for my communications course.
examples.zh: 为了完成传播课的作业，我跟岗观察了一名「应急调度」团队成员。

examples.en: The city's emergency dispatch system recorded when each crew was assigned to the incident.
examples.zh: 市里的「应急调度」系统记录了每支救援队接到此次任务的时间。

words.enDefinition: to send an available team or vehicle to an incident

examples.en: The control room agreed to dispatch a unit to the residence hall entrance.
examples.zh: 指挥室同意「派出应急单位」前往宿舍楼入口。

examples.en: The call handler gathered enough information to dispatch a unit to the correct building.
examples.zh: 接线员收集了足够的信息，好「派出应急单位」前往正确的楼栋。

collocations: dispatch a unit to the scene
dispatch a unit to an address

words.enDefinition: a crew or vehicle assigned to respond to a particular incident

examples.en: The responding unit reached the building from the quieter side street behind campus.
examples.zh: 「出勤的应急单位」从校园后面较安静的小街抵达了这栋楼。

examples.en: The dispatcher passed the updated entrance details to the responding unit by radio.
examples.zh: 调度员通过无线电向「出勤的应急单位」补充了最新的入口信息。

words.enDefinition: present at the place where an incident occurred

examples.en: The dispatcher confirmed that the crew was on scene when I called again.
examples.zh: 我再次打电话时，调度员确认救援队「已到现场」。

examples.en: An officer was already on scene when the building manager arrived from home.
examples.zh: 楼宇管理员从家里赶到时，已有一位警员「到现场」。

words.enDefinition: travelling toward a place and having not yet arrived

examples.en: The campus security officer was en route when I noticed the gate was locked.
examples.zh: 我发现大门锁着时，校园安保人员还「在路上」。

examples.en: The crew received the new room number while en route to the hall.
examples.zh: 救援队「在赶往宿舍楼的路上」收到了更新后的房间号。

words.enDefinition: the place where an incident happened or is happening

examples.en: The caller identified the incident location as a bus stop outside the library.
examples.zh: 来电者说「事件发生地点」是图书馆外的一个公交站。

examples.en: The dispatcher marked the incident location on a map beside the caller's address.
examples.zh: 调度员在地图上把「事件发生地点」标在来电者地址的旁边。

words.enDefinition: the place from which a person is making a call

examples.en: The map showed the caller location on the opposite side of the river.
examples.zh: 地图显示「来电者所在位置」在河对岸。

examples.en: The screen listed the caller location separately from the reported incident address downtown.
examples.zh: 屏幕分别列出了「来电者所在位置」和市中心的事发地址。

words.enDefinition: the precise place where a person or thing is situated

examples.en: Mina described the exact location of the locked gate using a nearby sign.
examples.zh: 米娜借助附近的标志说明了锁着的那扇门的「确切位置」。

examples.en: The operator confirmed our exact location before sending a message to the crew.
examples.zh: 接线员先确认了我们的「确切位置」，随后给救援队发了消息。

words.enDefinition: a marker on a digital map showing one particular point

examples.en: I saved the location pin for the footpath entrance when the group stopped.
examples.zh: 大家停下来时，我保存了步道入口的「地图位置标记」。

examples.en: The location pin showed the east entrance instead of the main campus gate.
examples.zh: 「地图位置标记」显示的是东入口，而不是校园正门。

words.enDefinition: sending one's current position to another person through a device

examples.en: Our group used location sharing to tell the residence adviser where we were waiting.
examples.zh: 我们这组用了「位置共享」，让宿舍辅导员知道我们在哪里等。

examples.en: My battery warned me just after I turned off location sharing on the way home.
examples.zh: 我回家路上刚关闭「位置共享」，手机就提示电量不足。

words.zhGloss: 供调度的来电确切位置
words.enDefinition: a validated US street address with any extra details needed to locate the caller
acceptedZhAnswers: 供调度的来电确切位置

examples.en: The training example included a room number as part of the dispatchable location.
examples.zh: 培训示例里的「供调度的来电确切位置」包含房间号。

examples.en: The US campus phone system sends a dispatchable location with calls from the library.
examples.zh: 从图书馆打电话时，这所美国大学的校园电话系统会随通话发送「供调度的来电确切位置」。

words.enDefinition: an address identifying a building by its street and number

examples.en: The caretaker gave the street address of the workshop from the posted contact sheet.
examples.zh: 管理员照着张贴的联络表，说出了工场的「街道门牌地址」。

examples.en: The street address on the west gate belongs to the building next door.
examples.zh: 西门上的「街道门牌地址」是隔壁那栋楼的。

words.enDefinition: the place closest to someone where two or more roads meet

examples.en: The driver reported the nearest intersection because the road had no house numbers.
examples.zh: 这条路没有门牌，司机便报了「最近的道路交叉口」。

examples.en: The campus map marked the nearest intersection just beyond the visitor parking lot.
examples.zh: 校园地图标出了「最近的道路交叉口」，就在访客停车场过去一点。

words.enDefinition: a street that crosses the main street used to identify a location

examples.en: The call handler asked for a cross street to narrow down the location.
examples.zh: 接线员问了离现场较近的一条「相交的街道」，以缩小定位范围。

examples.en: The driver named the cross street printed on a sign opposite the bus stop.
examples.zh: 司机报出了公交站对面路牌上那条「相交的街道」的名字。

words.enDefinition: the closest distinctive place or object that helps identify where someone is

examples.en: The clock tower was the nearest landmark we could see from the field.
examples.zh: 钟楼是我们从运动场能看到的「最近的显眼地标」。

examples.en: I described the nearest landmark first because I couldn't read the street sign.
examples.zh: 我看不清路牌，就先说明了「最近的显眼地标」。

words.enDefinition: a sign on or beside a street showing its name or information

examples.en: We read the street sign aloud to make sure we had the right spelling.
examples.zh: 我们把「街道标识牌」上的街名念了出来，确保拼写正确。

examples.en: The shop awning partly covered the street sign at the end of the block.
examples.zh: 街区尽头的「街道标识牌」被商店的遮阳篷挡住了一部分。

words.enDefinition: where two or more roads or paths meet

examples.en: We waited at the junction of Park Road and the university service road.
examples.zh: 我们等候的地点是「公园路和大学后勤通道的交会处」。

examples.en: A member of staff stood at the junction of the footpath and the driveway.
examples.zh: 一名工作人员站在「步道和车道的交会处」。

collocations: at the junction of two roads
at the junction of two paths
at the junction of the road and the driveway

words.enDefinition: a road sign indicating distance measured in miles along a route

examples.en: The passenger read the mile marker out loud as the van slowed down.
examples.zh: 面包车减速时，那名乘客大声报出了「英里里程标」上的数字。

examples.en: Our rideshare driver described the nearest mile marker and the colour of the car.
examples.zh: 网约车司机报了最近的「英里里程标」，并说了车的颜色。

words.enDefinition: a point where a motorway joins another road by ramps

examples.en: The traffic report gave the number of the motorway junction nearest the incident.
examples.zh: 路况播报说出了离事发地点最近的「高速公路互通口」编号。

examples.en: Our bus passed the motorway junction just before the driver stopped for assistance.
examples.zh: 司机停车求助前，我们的长途车刚经过「高速公路互通口」。

words.enDefinition: a ramp or turn that lets traffic leave a major road

examples.en: The passenger told the operator which highway exit the bus had just passed.
examples.zh: 乘客告诉接线员，大巴刚刚经过了哪个「公路出口」。

examples.en: The tow truck waited near the highway exit at the edge of town.
examples.zh: 拖车在城镇边缘的「公路出口」附近等着。

words.enDefinition: travelling or leading in the direction of north

examples.en: The caller said the broken-down coach was blocking one northbound lane near campus.
examples.zh: 来电者说，抛锚的大巴堵住了校园附近一条「向北行驶的」车道。

examples.en: Our northbound train was held at the station while staff checked the platform.
examples.zh: 工作人员检查站台时，我们乘坐的「北行」列车在车站暂时停留。

words.enDefinition: travelling or leading in the direction of south

examples.en: The radio report said the southbound carriageway had reopened after the morning crash.
examples.zh: 广播说，早上的撞车事故过后，「向南行驶的」一侧车道已重新开放。

examples.en: The emergency crew was approaching from the southbound side of the main road.
examples.zh: 救援队正从主路「向南行驶的」一侧过来。

words.enDefinition: the part of a road used by vehicles, sometimes for one direction only

examples.en: The wrecked bicycle lay on the edge of the carriageway beside the bus stop.
examples.zh: 损坏的自行车倒在公交站旁「公路行车路面」的边缘。

examples.en: The police closed one carriageway while officers spoke to the drivers involved.
examples.zh: 警方暂时封闭了一侧「行车路面」，警员向涉事司机了解情况。

words.enDefinition: a paved strip beside a motorway used mainly for emergencies

examples.en: The coach stayed on the hard shoulder until the breakdown assistance team arrived.
examples.zh: 大巴停在「硬路肩」上，直到道路救援队赶来。

examples.en: I could see flashing lights on the hard shoulder beyond the next bend.
examples.zh: 我能看到下一个弯道过去一点的「硬路肩」上有灯在闪。

words.enDefinition: a smaller road running beside a major road or providing local access to facilities

examples.en: The caller said the stalled van was on the service road beside campus.
examples.zh: 来电者说，抛锚的货车停在校园旁的「辅路」上。

examples.en: The front desk pointed the crew toward the service road behind the laboratory.
examples.zh: 前台人员给救援队指了实验楼后面的「辅路」。

words.enDefinition: a road that provides a way into a particular property or site

examples.en: The staff member waited at the start of the access road beside the sports field.
examples.zh: 工作人员在运动场旁的「进出通道」入口等候。

examples.en: A barrier on the access road prevented vehicles from reaching the rear entrance.
examples.zh: 「进出通道」上的路障挡住了车辆，后门开不过去。

words.enDefinition: an entrance normally used by workers or deliveries rather than the public

examples.en: The caretaker unlocked the service entrance so the crew could reach the lower floor.
examples.zh: 管理员打开「后勤出入口」，让救援队能到下一层。

examples.en: Our building plan shows the service entrance behind the row of bicycle racks.
examples.zh: 我们楼的平面图显示，「后勤出入口」在那排自行车架后面。

words.enDefinition: an entrance used for bringing goods into or out of a building

examples.en: The porter waited beside the loading entrance because the front doors were locked.
examples.zh: 正门锁着，门房就在「货物装卸入口」旁等。

examples.en: The van was parked outside the loading entrance at the back of the library.
examples.zh: 那辆货车停在图书馆后面的「货物装卸入口」外。

words.enDefinition: the principal gate through which people or vehicles enter a site

examples.en: The security guard met the responding crew at the main gate shortly after dark.
examples.zh: 天刚黑不久，安保人员就在「正门」和救援队会合。

examples.en: From the bus stop, I could see the main gate beside the flagpoles.
examples.zh: 从公交站可以看到旗杆旁的「正门」。

words.enDefinition: a gate for people entering or leaving on foot

examples.en: The pedestrian gate near the library stayed open while the road gate was closed.
examples.zh: 路口的车行门关着时，图书馆附近的「行人门」仍然开着。

examples.en: I met the caretaker by the pedestrian gate on the quieter side of campus.
examples.zh: 我在校园较安静一侧的「行人门」旁和管理员会合。

words.enDefinition: a number used to identify one level of a building

examples.en: The dispatcher repeated the floor number to make sure she had heard it correctly.
examples.zh: 调度员复述了「楼层号」，确认自己没有听错。

examples.en: The building directory lists the floor number next to each department's name upstairs.
examples.zh: 楼内导览牌把「楼层号」标在对应的部门名称旁边。

words.enDefinition: a flat area at the top of or between flights of stairs

examples.en: She waited on the landing outside our floor while I found the caretaker.
examples.zh: 我去找管理员时，她在我们那层外面的「楼梯平台」上等。

examples.en: The nearest room number was painted on the door facing the landing upstairs.
examples.zh: 最近的房间号刷在楼上正对「楼梯平台」的门上。

words.enDefinition: the level at or roughly even with the ground outside a building

examples.en: The accessible entrance is at ground level beside the ramp near the road.
examples.zh: 无障碍入口在路边坡道旁的「地面层」。

examples.en: The staff member waited at ground level while her colleague checked the basement.
examples.zh: 工作人员在「地面层」等，同事去查看地下室。

words.enDefinition: at a position lower than the surface of the ground

examples.en: The storage area is below ground, directly under the university's large lecture theatre.
examples.zh: 储藏区「在地面以下」，位于学校大阶梯教室正下方。

examples.en: Our phone signal got weaker once we went below ground in the station.
examples.zh: 我们在车站走到「地面以下」后，手机信号变弱了。

words.enDefinition: on the other side of the street from a place

examples.en: We're waiting across the street from the residence hall, beside the bus shelter.
examples.zh: 我们在「宿舍楼的街对面」等，就在公交候车亭旁。

examples.en: The pharmacy across the street from campus has a bright sign above its entrance.
examples.zh: 「校园街对面」的药店入口上方有一块很亮的招牌。

words.enDefinition: at the end of something that is furthest away

examples.en: The door is at the far end of the corridor, past the toilets.
examples.zh: 那扇门在「走廊的另一端尽头」，要走过洗手间。

examples.en: I saw a staff member waiting at the far end of the covered walkway.
examples.zh: 我看见一名工作人员在「有顶走道的另一端尽头」等着。

collocations: at the far end of the corridor
at the far end of the hall
at the far end of the platform

words.enDefinition: a short distance beyond a particular point or place

examples.en: Our group is waiting just past the clock tower beside a low brick wall.
examples.zh: 我们这组在「刚过钟楼一点」的矮砖墙旁等。

examples.en: The entrance you want is just past the campus bookshop on the right.
examples.zh: 你找的入口在「过了校园书店一点」的右手边。

words.enDefinition: facing the point where people enter a place

examples.en: I'm standing opposite the entrance to the library, beside the green recycling bins.
examples.zh: 我站在「图书馆入口对面」，就在绿色的回收桶旁。

examples.en: The responders parked opposite the entrance because the driveway was closed that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚车道关闭了，救援队就把车停「在入口对面」。

words.enDefinition: a list or sign showing where rooms or organizations are located inside a building

examples.en: The building directory showed a second entrance on the side facing the library.
examples.zh: 「楼内导览牌」显示，朝向图书馆的那一侧还有一个入口。

examples.en: I checked the building directory before telling the operator which floor we were on.
examples.zh: 我先看了「楼内导览牌」，才告诉接线员我们在哪一层。

words.enDefinition: to say the individual letters in the name of a street

examples.en: The operator asked me to spell the street name because it sounded unfamiliar.
examples.zh: 接线员没听过这条街，就请我「拼出街名」。

examples.en: Could you spell the street name again while I write the letters down?
examples.zh: 你能再「拼一遍街名」吗？我把字母记下来。

collocations: ask someone to spell the street name

words.enDefinition: to explain where you are in enough detail for someone to find you

examples.en: Can you describe your location using a building or sign that you can see?
examples.zh: 你能用看得见的楼或标志「说明你所在的位置」吗？

examples.en: The operator asked, "Could you describe your location without using the room number?"
examples.zh: 接线员问：“你能不用房间号「说明你所在的位置」吗？”

collocations: describe your location over the phone

words.enDefinition: to check that an address is correct

examples.en: Could you confirm the address so I can find the right entrance on my map?
examples.zh: 你能「核实一下地址」吗？这样我就能在地图上找到正确的入口。

examples.en: The dispatcher called again to confirm the address before updating the crew's route.
examples.zh: 调度员再次来电「核实地址」，然后更新了救援队的行进路线。

collocations: ask someone to confirm the address

words.enDefinition: not able to find a particular person, place, or thing

examples.en: The crew was unable to locate the entrance mentioned in the first call.
examples.zh: 救援队「找不到」第一次通话中提到的入口。

examples.en: The officer said he was unable to locate the building on his map.
examples.zh: 警员说他在地图上「找不到」那栋楼。

words.enDefinition: to meet emergency personnel when they arrive at or near the scene

examples.en: The caretaker went outside to meet the responders by the residence hall gate.
examples.zh: 管理员到外面，在宿舍楼大门旁「和救援人员会合」。

examples.en: I asked a classmate to meet the responders at the rear of the building.
examples.zh: 我请一名同学到楼后「和救援人员会合」。

collocations: meet the responders at the gate
go out to meet the responders

words.enDefinition: the count of people directly affected by or taking part in an incident

examples.en: The call handler asked about the number of people involved in the crash.
examples.zh: 接线员询问了这起撞车事故的「涉及人数」。

examples.en: The witness couldn't confirm the number of people involved from across the street.
examples.zh: 目击者隔着一条街，无法确认「涉及人数」。

collocations: confirm the number of people involved
report the number of people involved
estimate the number of people involved

words.enDefinition: someone who is present but not directly involved in an event

examples.en: A bystander outside the gym offered the caller a quieter place to speak.
examples.zh: 体育馆外的一名「现场旁观者」让来电者到一个较安静的地方说话。

examples.en: The officer took down the name of a bystander on the opposite pavement.
examples.zh: 警员记下了对面人行道上一名「现场旁观者」的姓名。

words.enDefinition: a person who saw an event happen

examples.en: The dispatcher asked whether the caller was an eyewitness to the incident outside.
examples.zh: 调度员问来电者是不是外面那件事的「亲眼目击者」。

examples.en: The first eyewitness described what she saw from the front of the bus.
examples.zh: 第一位「亲眼目击者」描述了她在车头看到的情况。

words.enDefinition: to notify the appropriate people or services of an urgent incident

examples.en: The night porter used the desk phone to report an emergency in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 夜间门卫用值班台的电话「报告了紧急情况」，地点是院子。

examples.en: Residents can use the posted number to report an emergency on the premises.
examples.zh: 如果楼内出现紧急情况，住户可以拨打张贴的电话「报告紧急情况」。

words.enDefinition: an urgent incident that is still happening and requires a response

examples.en: The receptionist asked whether it was an active emergency or something from earlier.
examples.zh: 前台人员问，这是「仍在发生的紧急情况」，还是之前发生的事。

examples.en: The dispatcher received a new call about the same active emergency outside campus.
examples.zh: 调度员又接到一通电话，报告校外同一起「仍在发生的紧急情况」。

words.enDefinition: a threat that could cause harm right away

examples.en: The call handler asked whether anyone on the platform was in immediate danger.
examples.zh: 接线员询问站台上有没有人正面临「眼前的危险」。

examples.en: The updated message said nobody was in immediate danger at the residence hall.
examples.zh: 更新后的消息说，宿舍楼内无人面临「眼前的危险」。

words.enDefinition: the kind of urgent situation or problem being reported

examples.en: The operator asked about the nature of the emergency before transferring my call.
examples.zh: 接线员先问了「紧急情况的性质」，然后转接了我的电话。

examples.en: The record describes the nature of the emergency in the caller's own words.
examples.zh: 记录用来电者自己的话说明了「紧急情况的性质」。

collocations: describe the nature of the emergency
confirm the nature of the emergency
ask about the nature of the emergency

words.enDefinition: a question asking whether any person has been injured

examples.en: Is anyone hurt at the entrance where the two vehicles came to a stop?
examples.zh: 两辆车停下的那个入口附近，「有人受伤吗」？

examples.en: Is anyone hurt, or has everybody already walked back to the reception area?
examples.zh: 「有人受伤吗」？还是大家已经都走回接待区了？

collocations: is anyone hurt in the car
is anyone hurt at the scene

words.enDefinition: to tell someone your name or role so they know who you are

examples.en: The operator said, "Please identify yourself before I transfer you to the duty officer."
examples.zh: 接线员说：“请先「说明你的身份」，我再把你转接给值班警员。”

examples.en: You can identify yourself as the residence adviser when the dispatcher answers the call.
examples.zh: 调度员接通时，你可以「说明你是」这栋宿舍的辅导员。

words.enDefinition: a person who places a phone call

examples.en: The caller stayed near the bus shelter where reception was better that night.
examples.zh: 那晚公交候车亭附近信号更好，「来电者」就留在那里。

examples.en: A second caller gave the same street name but a different house number.
examples.zh: 第二位「来电者」报出的街名相同，但门牌号不同。

words.enDefinition: a call that is being received on a phone

examples.en: I picked up an incoming call while my friend waited beside the campus gate.
examples.zh: 朋友在校园大门旁等着时，我接了一个「呼入电话」。

examples.en: The desk phone rang again for an incoming call from the control room.
examples.zh: 值班电话又响了，这次是控制室的「呼入电话」。

words.enDefinition: to stay able to respond or be contacted if needed

examples.en: The officer asked the witness to remain available by phone through the afternoon.
examples.zh: 警员请目击者下午「继续保持联络畅通」。

examples.en: I agreed to remain available while the crew looked for the correct campus entrance.
examples.zh: 我答应「继续保持联络畅通」，等救援队找到正确的校园入口。

words.enDefinition: to pronounce words so the listener can understand them easily

examples.en: I moved away from the crowd so I could speak clearly on the phone.
examples.zh: 我走到离人群远点的地方，好在电话里「说清楚一些」。

examples.en: The volunteer reminded us to speak clearly when reading out the building name.
examples.zh: 志愿者提醒我们念出楼名时要「说清楚一些」。

words.enDefinition: to ask the same question again, usually to make sure it was heard

examples.en: Could you repeat the question while I move away from the traffic noise?
examples.zh: 你能「把问题再说一遍」吗？我先离车流远一点。

examples.en: I asked the call handler to repeat the question because the train was loud.
examples.zh: 列车噪声太大，我请接线员「把问题再说一遍」。

collocations: ask someone to repeat the question

words.enDefinition: to say the letters of a word individually for the listener

examples.en: I offered to spell it out when she asked how to write the street name.
examples.zh: 她问街名怎么写，我就主动提出「逐个字母拼出来」。

examples.en: Could you spell it out slowly so I get the building name right?
examples.zh: 你能慢慢地「逐个字母拼出来」吗？我想把楼名记对。

collocations: spell it out letter by letter

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying that the other person's voice cannot be heard

examples.en: I can't hear you over the engine, so let me step outside first.
examples.zh: 引擎太响，「我听不见你说话」，我先到外面去。

examples.en: I can't hear you clearly where I am, but my friend can take the phone.
examples.zh: 我在这里「听不清你说话」，但我朋友可以接电话。

collocations: I can't hear you over the noise
I'm afraid I can't hear you

words.enDefinition: the disappearance of a signal needed for a connection or transmission

examples.en: We experienced signal loss in the concrete stairwell and could no longer hear the operator.
examples.zh: 我们在混凝土楼梯间遇到了「信号丢失」，听不到接线员的声音了。

examples.en: The temporary signal loss ended as soon as the bus left the tunnel.
examples.zh: 公交车一出隧道，短暂的「信号丢失」就结束了。

words.enDefinition: a weak phone or radio signal causing communication problems

examples.en: The front desk has poor reception, so I took the call in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 前台「信号接收不良」，所以我到院子里接了电话。

examples.en: Because of poor reception in the basement, the operator had trouble hearing my address.
examples.zh: 地下室「信号接收不良」，接线员很难听清我报的地址。

words.enDefinition: a phrase meaning the call connection stopped carrying sound

examples.en: I heard a voice for a moment before the line went dead without warning.
examples.zh: 我听到了一小会儿人声，接着「电话突然没声了」。

examples.en: The operator had just asked for the postcode when the line went dead.
examples.zh: 接线员刚问了邮编，「电话就突然没声了」。

words.enDefinition: to lose a telephone connection before the conversation is finished

examples.en: If we get cut off, the front desk has my building and room number.
examples.zh: 要是我们「通话中断」，前台留有我的楼号和房号。

examples.en: I didn't want to get cut off again while moving between the two buildings.
examples.zh: 我不想在穿过两栋楼之间时再一次「通话中断」。

words.enDefinition: a phrase meaning a telephone call connects to the intended recipient

examples.en: When the call goes through, you'll hear the front desk recording before anyone answers.
examples.zh: 「电话接通」后，会先听到前台的录音，再有人接听。

examples.en: He stays by the window until the call goes through to the duty officer.
examples.zh: 他一直待在窗边，直到电话「接通」值班人员。

collocations: wait until the call goes through
the call goes through to reception

words.enDefinition: to play a call aloud through the phone's speaker

examples.en: We can put the call on speaker so everybody hears which entrance she means.
examples.zh: 我们可以「开免提」，这样大家都听得出她指的是哪个入口。

examples.en: I asked him to put the call on speaker so the caretaker could hear too.
examples.zh: 我请他「开免提」，好让管理员也能听到。

collocations: ask to be put on speaker

words.enDefinition: to make a telephone line available for other calls

examples.en: The receptionist moved a routine call to another phone to free up the line.
examples.zh: 前台接待员把一通普通电话转到另一部电话上，好「腾出电话线路」。

examples.en: I used my mobile to free up the line at the busy front desk.
examples.zh: 我改用手机，好给忙碌的前台「腾出电话线路」。

collocations: free up the line for incoming calls
move a routine call to free up the line

words.enDefinition: to pick up a call made in response to an earlier call

examples.en: I stepped away from the entrance to answer a callback from the campus office.
examples.zh: 我走到离入口远一点的地方，「接听校园办公室回拨的电话」。

examples.en: She kept her phone nearby so she could answer a callback from the control room.
examples.zh: 她把手机放在身边，以便「接听控制室回拨的电话」。

collocations: be ready to answer a callback
step outside to answer a callback

words.enDefinition: to have one's call connected to another person or department

examples.en: I asked to be put through to the duty officer at the residence hall.
examples.zh: 我请对方把电话「转接到」宿舍楼的值班人员那里。

examples.en: I expected to be put through to the campus desk after the announcement.
examples.zh: 我以为听完语音提示后会「被转接到」校园值班台。

collocations: be put through to an operator

words.enDefinition: to send a connected telephone call to another person or number

examples.en: The dispatcher stayed with me long enough to transfer the call to the right desk.
examples.zh: 调度员一直和我保持通话，直到「转接电话」到正确的值班台。

examples.en: Let me transfer the call to the person covering your part of campus tonight.
examples.zh: 我来「转接电话」，让今晚负责你那片校园的人接听。

collocations: transfer the call to another department
transfer the call to a colleague
ask someone to transfer the call

words.enDefinition: an audio record of a conversation made over the phone

examples.en: The supervisor checked the call recording to confirm when the address was given.
examples.zh: 主管听了「通话录音」，确认对方是什么时候报出地址的。

examples.en: The call recording captured the operator reading the room number back to the caller.
examples.zh: 「通话录音」录下了接线员向来电者复述房间号的声音。

words.enDefinition: a phone number for matters that do not need immediate emergency help

examples.en: The local police non-emergency number was printed beside the campus security desk details.
examples.zh: 当地警方的「非紧急联系电话」印在校园安保值班台联系方式旁。

examples.en: The student rang the non-emergency number to ask about a report filed last week.
examples.zh: 那名学生拨打「非紧急联系电话」，询问上周提交的一份报告。

words.enDefinition: a line of incoming calls waiting for available staff

examples.en: The front desk's call queue grew as families tried to reach the campus office.
examples.zh: 家属纷纷尝试联系校园办公室，前台的「来电等候队列」越来越长。

examples.en: A recorded message told callers their position in the call queue before answering.
examples.zh: 电话接通前，录音会告知来电者在「来电等候队列」中的位置。

words.enDefinition: to stay on the line until someone or another service answers

examples.en: A short recorded message played while I had to wait to be connected.
examples.zh: 我「等候接通」时，听到了一段简短的录音。

examples.en: The voice told me to wait to be connected to the local control room.
examples.zh: 语音提示我「等候接通」当地控制室。

collocations: wait to be connected to an operator
wait to be connected to the local office

words.enDefinition: a list recording calls made or received and their details

examples.en: The supervisor checked the call log for the time of the first report.
examples.zh: 主管在「通话记录」里查询第一次收到报告的时间。

examples.en: My phone's call log showed two missed calls from the residence office that evening.
examples.zh: 手机的「通话记录」显示，那天傍晚宿管办公室打来两次电话，我都没接到。

words.enDefinition: a reference number assigned to an incident in an official system

examples.en: The campus dispatcher gave me an incident number when I requested a follow-up.
examples.zh: 我要求了解后续情况时，校园调度员给了我一个「事件编号」。

examples.en: I wrote the incident number in my notes next to the time of the call.
examples.zh: 我把「事件编号」记在笔记里，写在通话时间旁边。

words.enDefinition: an emergency call that was placed unintentionally

examples.en: The call handler logged it as an accidental emergency call after speaking to me.
examples.zh: 接线员与我通话后，将其记录为一次「误拨紧急电话」。

examples.en: Staff discussed what an accidental emergency call looked like during the orientation session.
examples.zh: 迎新会上，工作人员解释了什么情况属于「误拨紧急电话」。

collocations: respond to an accidental emergency call

words.enDefinition: to call someone accidentally when a phone is pressed in a pocket or bag

examples.en: I managed to pocket dial my flatmate twice while cycling back from the station.
examples.zh: 我从车站骑车回来时，「手机在兜里误拨」了室友的电话两次。

examples.en: An unlocked screen can cause you to pocket dial a contact without noticing.
examples.zh: 屏幕没锁，你可能会不知不觉地「让手机在兜里误拨」联系人。

words.zhGloss: 重复报同一事件的来电
words.enDefinition: a separate call reporting an incident that has already been reported
acceptedZhAnswers: 重复报同一事件的来电

examples.en: The dispatcher linked the duplicate call to the report already on her screen.
examples.zh: 调度员把这通「重复报同一事件的来电」关联到了屏幕上已有的报告。

examples.en: I knew mine might be a duplicate call because another student was already talking.
examples.zh: 另一名学生已经在通话，我知道自己的电话可能是「重复报同一事件的来电」。

collocations: link a duplicate call to an incident

words.enDefinition: a service that accepts requests for emergency help by text message

examples.en: The accessibility guide explains where the emergency text service is available to visitors.
examples.zh: 无障碍指南说明了访客可以在哪里使用「紧急短信求助服务」。

examples.en: The support worker checked whether the emergency text service covered our part of town.
examples.zh: 助理查了一下「紧急短信求助服务」是否覆盖我们所在的城区。

words.enDefinition: a US service in participating areas for contacting 911 by text

examples.en: The county's accessibility page states whether text-to-911 is available in this part of town.
examples.zh: 县里的无障碍网页说明，这片城区是否提供「短信联系911服务」。

examples.en: Our orientation guide discussed text-to-911 in the section on accessible emergency communications.
examples.zh: 我们的迎新指南在应急通信无障碍章节中介绍了「短信联系911服务」。

words.enDefinition: text communication in which characters appear to the other person as they are typed

examples.en: The phone's accessibility menu showed real-time text beside the other calling options.
examples.zh: 手机的无障碍菜单把「实时文字通话」列在其他通话选项旁边。

examples.en: The demonstration showed how real-time text appears letter by letter on the operator's screen.
examples.zh: 演示展示了「实时文字通话」如何逐个字符显示在接线员屏幕上。

words.enDefinition: a service connecting sign language and spoken language through a video interpreter

examples.en: The interpreter on video relay signed while the call handler spoke over the phone.
examples.zh: 接线员在电话里说话时，「视频中继通话」服务的译员用手语转达。

examples.en: We watched a video relay demonstration during a session on accessible campus services.
examples.zh: 在介绍校园无障碍服务的活动上，我们看了「视频中继通话」演示。

words.enDefinition: a service that relays a conversation between typed text and speech

examples.en: Our residence handbook lists text relay under its options for accessible telephone calls.
examples.zh: 我们的宿舍手册把「文字中继通话」列在无障碍通话选项中。

examples.en: The front desk worker was familiar with text relay and waited for the reply.
examples.zh: 前台工作人员熟悉「文字中继通话」，便等对方回复。

words.enDefinition: a person who relays messages between callers using different modes of communication

examples.en: The relay operator read each typed message aloud to the person at reception.
examples.zh: 「中继话务员」把每条打出来的消息念给前台接听的人。

examples.en: I paused so the relay operator could finish passing my answer to the caller.
examples.zh: 我停了一下，让「中继话务员」把我的回答完整转达给来电者。

words.enDefinition: an interpreter who translates spoken conversation over the phone

examples.en: The dispatcher connected a telephone interpreter after I gave the name of my language.
examples.zh: 我报出自己使用的语言后，调度员接通了一名「电话口译员」。

examples.en: The telephone interpreter asked one person to speak at a time during the conversation.
examples.zh: 交谈时，「电话口译员」请大家一个一个说。

words.enDefinition: to bring an interpreter into a call so people can understand each other

examples.en: The operator offered to connect an interpreter after we explained which language we spoke.
examples.zh: 我们说明自己说哪种语言后，接线员提出可以「为通话接入口译员」。

examples.en: The front desk asked whether it could connect an interpreter while I waited on hold.
examples.zh: 我在线等候时，前台问能不能「为通话接入口译员」。

collocations: connect an interpreter to the call
wait for staff to connect an interpreter

words.enDefinition: a degree of hearing loss that can affect communication

examples.en: The student with a hearing impairment chose written messages at the busy reception desk.
examples.zh: 前台很忙，那名有「听力障碍」的学生选择通过文字交流。

examples.en: The operator asked what communication method worked best for the caller's hearing impairment.
examples.zh: 接线员询问哪种沟通方式最适合这位有「听力障碍」的来电者。

words.enDefinition: a difficulty that affects the ability to produce clear speech

examples.en: A speech impairment made it harder for him to say the unfamiliar street name.
examples.zh: 由于「言语障碍」，他说出那条陌生的街名更费力。

examples.en: The student with a speech impairment asked to type the details on her phone.
examples.zh: 有「言语障碍」的学生问能不能在手机上打字说明情况。

words.enDefinition: a person who interprets between a signed language and another language

examples.en: The university arranged for a sign language interpreter to attend the safety briefing.
examples.zh: 学校安排了一名「手语口译员」参加安全说明会。

examples.en: A sign language interpreter helped the visitor understand the questions from campus staff.
examples.zh: 一名「手语口译员」帮助访客理解校方工作人员提出的问题。

words.enDefinition: a button that connects a person to assistance during an emergency

examples.en: The emergency call button was clearly marked beside the lift controls in my residence.
examples.zh: 我的宿舍里，电梯控制面板旁清楚标示着「紧急呼叫按钮」。

examples.en: We recognised the symbol for the emergency call button from our access guide.
examples.zh: 我们认出了「紧急呼叫按钮」的标志，无障碍通行指南上见过。

words.enDefinition: an outdoor emergency telephone marked by a visible blue light

examples.en: A blue-light emergency phone stood near the bus stop beside the science building.
examples.zh: 科学楼旁的公交站附近设有一部「蓝灯紧急求助电话」。

examples.en: The campus map shows a blue-light emergency phone at each end of the walkway.
examples.zh: 校园地图显示，步道两端各有一部「蓝灯紧急求助电话」。

words.enDefinition: a two-way communication device for speaking to staff in an emergency

examples.en: The porter answered through the emergency intercom next to the parking lift doors.
examples.zh: 门房通过停车场电梯门旁的「紧急对讲装置」应答。

examples.en: The label on the emergency intercom identified the team that answers calls overnight.
examples.zh: 「紧急对讲装置」上的标签写明了夜间负责接听的团队。

words.enDefinition: the university service that receives reports and coordinates campus safety responders

examples.en: I called campus dispatch to ask which office was handling the earlier report.
examples.zh: 我联系了「校园安保调度」，询问之前的报告由哪个办公室处理。

examples.en: The officer checked in with campus dispatch after meeting the caretaker outside the library.
examples.zh: 警员在图书馆外与管理员会合后，向「校园安保调度」报了情况。

words.enDefinition: the phone number of a designated person to be contacted in an emergency

examples.en: The residence form still showed my old emergency contact number from last year.
examples.zh: 宿舍登记表上仍写着去年留下的旧「紧急联系人电话」。

examples.en: I checked that my emergency contact number included the international dialling code for home.
examples.zh: 我确认了自己的「紧急联系人电话」里有老家的国际区号。

words.enDefinition: to inform the person designated to be told about an emergency

examples.en: The residence adviser asked whether she should notify an emergency contact for me.
examples.zh: 宿舍辅导员问我，要不要帮我「通知紧急联系人」。

examples.en: The staff member had the details needed to notify an emergency contact that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，工作人员掌握了「通知紧急联系人」所需的信息。

collocations: ask to notify an emergency contact
notify an emergency contact by phone
permission to notify an emergency contact

words.enDefinition: a card listing whom to contact if the person carrying it needs assistance

examples.en: My emergency contact card lists both my residence office and my sister's phone number.
examples.zh: 我的「紧急联络信息卡」上有宿管办公室和我姐姐的电话号码。

examples.en: I replaced my emergency contact card after changing rooms and getting a new number.
examples.zh: 我换了房间和电话号码后，换了一张「紧急联络信息卡」。

collocations: fill in an emergency contact card

words.enDefinition: to tell the person on the phone something that helps them feel less worried

examples.en: The operator spoke slowly to reassure the caller while checking the address on screen.
examples.zh: 接线员一边在屏幕上核对地址，一边慢慢地说话「安抚来电者」。

examples.en: The call handler tried to reassure the caller that the crew had the information.
examples.zh: 接线员试着「安抚来电者」，告诉对方救援队已收到信息。

collocations: reassure the caller that help is coming

words.enDefinition: to ask additional personnel to come and help with an incident

examples.en: The supervisor told the officer to call for backup during the stadium training exercise.
examples.zh: 体育场训练演习期间，主管让警员「呼叫增援」。

examples.en: The campus officer used the radio to call for backup near the bus terminal.
examples.zh: 校园警员在公交总站附近通过无线电「呼叫增援」。

collocations: ask someone to call for backup

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying that people who will provide help are travelling to the scene

examples.en: She said assistance is on the way before asking me about the building entrance.
examples.zh: 她先说「救援人员已经在路上」，然后问我楼的入口在哪里。

examples.en: The update said assistance is on the way from the nearest available campus team.
examples.zh: 最新消息说，最近的一支可用校园「救援队已经在路上」。

collocations: confirm assistance is on the way
you can tell them assistance is on the way
assistance is already on the way

words.enDefinition: an address entered or given that does not match the intended location

examples.en: I realised I had given the wrong address after checking the name above the door.
examples.zh: 我看了门上方的名称后，才发现自己「把地址弄错了」。

examples.en: The first crew was sent to the wrong address on another street downtown.
examples.zh: 第一支救援队被派到了市中心另一条街上的一个「错误地址」。

words.enDefinition: a dialled telephone number that does not reach the person or service intended

examples.en: I realised I had the wrong number when a shop answered instead of the desk.
examples.zh: 接电话的是一家商店，我才发现「电话打错了」。

examples.en: The receptionist told me I'd dialled the wrong number for the campus safety office.
examples.zh: 接待员告诉我，联系校园安全办公室的「电话打错了」。

words.enDefinition: the systems and messages used to communicate during or about urgent incidents

examples.en: My class visited the university centre responsible for emergency communications on the main campus.
examples.zh: 我们班参观了主校区负责「应急通信」的大学中心。

examples.en: The accessibility committee discussed emergency communications with students who use different calling services.
examples.zh: 无障碍委员会与使用不同通话服务的学生讨论了「应急通信」。

words.enDefinition: the current stage or condition of an incident being handled

examples.en: The campus desk updated the incident status after hearing from the first crew.
examples.zh: 校园值班台收到第一支救援队的消息后，更新了「事件处理状态」。

examples.en: I quoted the reference number when asking about the incident status on Friday.
examples.zh: 我周五查询「事件处理状态」时，报了查询编号。

words.enDefinition: to require help to be provided straight away

examples.en: The dispatcher asked whether anyone inside the building would need immediate assistance that evening.
examples.zh: 调度员问，那天晚上楼内有没有人会「需要立即协助」。

examples.en: We need immediate assistance at the west gate, the caretaker told the operator.
examples.zh: 管理员对接线员说：“西门这边「需要立即协助」。”

collocations: tell someone you need immediate assistance
need immediate assistance at the scene

words.enDefinition: a designated place where emergency personnel can enter or reach a site

examples.en: The residence map marked an emergency access point beside the old bike racks.
examples.zh: 宿舍地图在旧自行车架旁标了一个「救援人员出入点」。

examples.en: The crew met campus staff at the emergency access point behind the sports hall.
examples.zh: 救援队在体育馆后面的「救援人员出入点」与校园工作人员会合。

collocations: keep an emergency access point clear

words.enDefinition: a hospital entrance set aside for arriving ambulances

examples.en: Our bus stopped across the road from the ambulance entrance at the hospital.
examples.zh: 我们乘坐的公交车停在医院「救护车专用入口」对面。

examples.en: The security guard pointed us toward a public door beyond the ambulance entrance.
examples.zh: 安保人员为我们指出了「救护车专用入口」那头的一扇公众入口。

words.enDefinition: a route or clearance that allows emergency vehicles to reach a location

examples.en: The orientation team moved their van away from the emergency vehicle access beside campus.
examples.zh: 迎新团队把面包车从校园旁的「应急车辆通道」挪开。

examples.en: The building plan marked emergency vehicle access between the loading bay and the gate.
examples.zh: 平面图在装卸区和大门之间标出了「应急车辆通道」。

words.enDefinition: a room where staff monitor incidents and coordinate a response

examples.en: The duty officer gave the control room an update after leaving the sports hall.
examples.zh: 值班警员离开体育馆后，向「调度控制室」通报了最新情况。

examples.en: Screens in the control room showed the locations of crews already on duty.
examples.zh: 「调度控制室」的屏幕显示着各值班小组的位置。

words.enDefinition: to use a radio to report one's status or whereabouts to a team

examples.en: The volunteer was asked to check in by radio after reaching the field entrance.
examples.zh: 志愿者到达运动场入口后，需要「用无线电报到」。

examples.en: The organiser heard each team check in by radio during the practice session.
examples.zh: 演练期间，组织者听见每支队伍「用无线电报到」。

collocations: check in by radio from the gate
ask someone to check in by radio

words.enDefinition: a handheld device used to send and receive voice messages by radio

examples.en: The campus officer picked up her radio handset before walking toward the rear gate.
examples.zh: 校园警员拿起「无线电对讲机」，朝后门走去。

examples.en: The caretaker could hear a message coming from the radio handset at reception.
examples.zh: 管理员听到前台的「无线电对讲机」传出消息。
